body:
The problem with this implementation is some objects have a ton of unnamed meshes without materials, and if I click the extract button, I'm going to end up with hundreds of the same blank material files extracted to the project, which I don't want.

So it would be nice to by default extract one material file, but then allow overriding materials.
I think the plan to move forward with this might be to finish up reduz' workflow for material editing from the 3D import dialog from here: #107351 - it adds some support for handling of unnamed materials.

Once we have the material editing dialog, we can then look again at this bug and see if it can be fixed in a way that will allow overriding materials per-mesh or per-material, without spitting out tons of empty material files when I extract all.

I was designing the import pipeline for my game from Blender to Godot, and I found this issue starting from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/64853 and reading all the related PRs and discussion. IMHO the fact that you can't set external materials for `` in the Advanced Import Settings is a **bug**. It currently results in no action and it's not what the user expects to happen. No warnings or errors either. More context: I plan to import in Godot multiple `.glb` files that share the same materials/textures. Using a vanilla export approach, Blender packs the material and the texture data in the `.glb` file. At import time in Godot, this results in unpacking the same texture over and over. This is unacceptable in any realistic production environment, as it pollutes the repository with duplicated data. The solution from the export pov is to change the export settings so that materials are not packed in the `.glb` file (in Blender you do `File → Export → glTF → Data → Material → Materials → Placeholder`). When importing in Godot, this obviously results in no duplicated textures/materials, which is desired. But material information is lost, resulting in the `` behaviour these proposals/PRs are all about. In the Advanced Import Settings every lost material slot maps to an ``: Here I already notice a difference between this PR and stable 4.6.1. Custom PR shows `Import ID: name_of_mesh_data@n` Version 4.6.1 shows `Import ID: @MATERIAL:n` I haven’t tried rebasing this PR yet and I'm not sure if this change makes the PR incompatible. The current state of the PR delivers exactly what it promises in only 9 lines of code. The alternative is a dormant ~460 LOC PR (with a superseded original PR from 2023) that nobody has discussed for 9 months https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107351. While I fully respect (and gladly desire) the implementation of the new Asset Import Dialog, I don't see how merging this right now is a blocker to the more advanced rework. At that time we can just strip these 9 lines away if that's superseded. From my understanding only one piece is missing. The last blocker seems to be the above @lyuma comment, stating that: > The problem with this implementation is some objects have a ton of unnamed meshes without materials, and if I click the extract button, I'm going to end up with hundreds of the same blank material files extracted to the project, which I don't want. I don't fully understand the later part when referring to overriding materials, so I’ll focus on the point above. I couldn’t find a test file to reproduce this behavior, so, based on that comment, I created a Blender file with multiple objects, with both no material assigned and others with materials. The white boxes have no material attached. The blue ones share the same material. Then I exported to `.glb` with the aforementioned placeholder material setting. I expect to see no _named_ materials in the imported `.glb` file in Godot. In fact, this is the result: I now try to extract the materials how @lyuma stated. This is the result: Pressing "Extract" results in **no** newly created material or resource. So, I'm not able to reproduce the claim that extracting unnamed materials results in creating multiple empty materials. The same in stable 4.6.1: still results in no materials created. Here I attach a couple of test projects for both 4.5 and 4.6.1: [unnamed-material-4.5.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26489356/unnamed-material-4.5.zip) [unnamed-material-4.6.1.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26489365/unnamed-material-4.6.1.zip) **Summary** In conclusion, once we settle the "extract materials" argument I don't see why this can't be merged. The current behavior is no feedback when assigning external materials to `` The expected behavior would be either allow assignment or show a warning/error. I don't think waiting for the _bigger_ rework is the way to address an issue we have right now that mines a sane material assigning workflow. This PR provides a minimal fix in ~9 LOC. Larger rework can still happen later and eventually scrape this fix that's just a few lines. For the future, the current workaround is to assign a material as an override in the scene mesh nodes.
